item.title: VelServe: Taming Decode Jitters in LLM Inference with Tail-Calibrated Scheduling
item.description:
VelServe introduces a tail‑calibrated scheduler that keeps large‑language‑model inference within latency targets by adding headroom for late steps, boosting goodput up to 4.4× over existing methods. It solves the problem of decode jitters that break service‑level objectives for streaming applications. The system was tested on Qwen3‑8B, DeepSeek variants and outperformed state‑of‑the‑art baselines.

IT Breakdown: If you manage LLM inference on multiple GPUs, use VelServe by calibrating each decode step’s prefill work based on its tail latency: 1) measure iteration latency tail, 2) set prefill budget to leave headroom for the SLO‑defined rare overrun, 3) prioritize shortest waiting prompts to minimise TTFT. This reduces SLO violations and increases throughput. If your workloads are not LLM‑based, this is not directly applicable.

item.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
item.description:
A new black‑box method splits a large language model’s uncertainty into prompt ambiguity (aleatoric) and true knowledge gaps (epistemic) using two nested ensembles of random decodings and prompt perturbations. It works with only sampling access, matches white‑box baselines on small QA tasks, and highlights when a model’s uncertainty comes from the prompt or from missing knowledge.

IT Breakdown: If you manage LLM‑based services, run two‑level ensembles: 1) sample multiple outputs for the same prompt, 2) apply small semantic changes to the prompt and sample again, 3) compute covariance to separate aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty. Use the results to adjust prompts or retrain when epistemic uncertainty is high.

item.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
item.description:
WeightBench is a benchmark that tests how well large language models can read, edit, and create neural network weights without using gradient descent. The researchers built 42 tasks covering reading, fixing, writing, recognising impossible edits, and data‑free compression across models from 2K to 7B parameters, and found that the best LLMs can write small control policies but still struggle with larger models and compression. This work is not directly relevant to typical cloud infrastructure management.

IT Breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work

item.title: [News] Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams
item.description: OpenAI introduces GPT‑6 Astra computer-use agents that automate multi-step healthcare workflows, such as prior authorizations and discharge planning, through the OpenAI API and ChatGPT for Clinicians. These agents can navigate multiple applications, draft clinical orders, and log audit trails while maintaining HIPAA compliance.

item.title: [News] LVMH’s Media Division announces strategic partnership with OpenAI
item.description: LVMH’s Media Division has signed a strategic partnership with OpenAI to deploy ChatGPT Enterprise across its publications, enabling AI‑driven journalism tools such as document research, comparison, and translation. The collaboration aims to boost content accessibility, personalization, and operational efficiency within LVMH’s media brands.
